cases.nominal_success_artifact: valid Checkout/Payment Mandates and signed Payment Receipt accepted by the relevant AP2 roles
cases.intended_consequence: the user received the intended commercial good/service under the intended terms
cases.reason: AP2 secures authorization/payment evidence and explicitly leaves commerce-protocol details outside its scope; payment authorization/receipt is not merchant-fulfillment proof.

cases.intended_consequence: the paid resource/service was actually delivered and usable for the request
cases.reason: x402 settlement establishes payment-side state from the resource-server perspective; settlement can represent different payment commitments and is separable from the resource postcondition.

cases.nominal_success_artifact: Stripe Refund state observed as succeeded
cases.intended_consequence: the intended refund is economically final and cannot subsequently reverse/fail
cases.reason: Stripe documents asynchronous refund behavior including tests in which a succeeded refund later fails; provider success must not be upgraded to economic finality.

cases.nominal_success_artifact: HTTP 202 Accepted from Kubernetes DELETE on an object with finalizers
cases.intended_consequence: the object and required dependents are actually gone
cases.reason: Kubernetes marks deletionTimestamp and returns 202 while finalizers can keep the object in Terminating until cleanup completes.

cases.intended_consequence: the target instance is terminally terminated and required attached resources have the intended disposition
cases.reason: EC2 returns an intermediate shutting-down state; termination can take time or become stuck, and attached-volume disposition depends on configuration.

cases.nominal_success_artifact: HTTP 202 Accepted from cancel workflow run
cases.intended_consequence: all execution attributable to the run has ceased and cannot continue producing side effects
cases.reason: GitHub documents a multi-step cancellation process; jobs/steps whose conditions remain true can continue, and forced termination occurs only after the cancellation timeout.

cases.nominal_success_artifact: HTTP 200 from an RFC 7009 token revocation endpoint
cases.intended_consequence: the relevant authorization is no longer usable at every resource boundary that matters
cases.reason: RFC 7009 uses 200 both for successful revocation and invalid tokens and acknowledges propagation delay; related-token revocation depends on server policy.

cases.nominal_success_artifact: successful deletion of a Google Cloud service-account key
cases.intended_consequence: credentials derived from that key can no longer authorize access
cases.reason: Google Cloud documents that deleting a service-account key does not revoke short-lived credentials already issued from that key.

notes: This corpus is intentionally outside-in and sourced from independent public protocols/APIs rather than RISU-authored fixtures.
The success artifacts are not assumed wrong; the test is whether they prove the broader intended consequence.
No case may be deleted or relabeled after arm outputs are inspected.
